subject: Hosted API - pricing qualification and token volume
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API - pricing qualification and token volume

Hi Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we can size pricing and capacity: 

Highlights from the call:
- Use case: customer support generation + short-context retrieval (avg prompt ~80 tokens, avg response ~120 tokens)
- Integration: hosted API, public internet (no VPC) to start; enterprise VPC later this year
- Success metrics: latency p95 < 500ms for single-turn generation; uptime SLA required for later stage

Pricing/volume asks (action items for you):
1) Confirm expected monthly token volume (rough order of magnitude is fine — daily active users x prompts/day x tokens)
2) Confirm expected peak TPS (requests per second) during peak hours
3) Share any target $/1M tokens or budget range we should aim for for initial sizing

What we can commit on our side for the next steps:
- I attached a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) and a quick spreadsheet template to capture your traffic assumptions. If you fill the spreadsheet we can turn this into a tailored quote and capacity plan.
- We can provision a small reserved slot (no commitment) to validate peak TPS in a short soak test next week if the numbers look right.

Planned next steps:
- Alex: reply with the ballpark monthly tokens + peak TPS and a budget range (if you have one) — by EOD Tue
- Sean: will draft preliminary unit economics and a target $/1M tokens for the volume band once Alex confirms numbers
- Marissa: put together the MAP and pricing draft based on inputs

Thanks again — small ask and we’ll follow up with a quote and a test plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachment: mutual_action_plan.pdf (1 page), acme_token_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet template)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeinc.com
Date: 2026-03-30T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - pricing qualification and token volume

Hey Marissa — thanks for the recap and the MAP. Quick answers from our side: 

- Expected monthly token volume (ballpark): ~120,000,000 tokens/month (120M) — this is initial production usage after launch; could grow 2-3x over 12 months.
- Peak TPS: ~8 TPS during peak windows (peak is ~30-45 min during daytime hours). Average TPS looks closer to 2.
- Budget range: we're thinking roughly $4k - $6k / month to start, but we can be flexible if unit economics make sense for our scale.

Also: procurement is copying in case they want to coordinate PO/terms. We may need a basic SOC 2 attestation before production, but that's not blocking the eval.

Let me know what you need from our end — I filled the spreadsheet and attached it to this reply.

Cheers,
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, Acme Inc.
alex.johnson@acmeinc.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, procurement@acmeinc.com
Date: 2026-03-30T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - pricing qualification and token volume

Thanks Alex — got the filled spreadsheet, appreciate the quick turnaround. Two quick clarifications so Sean can model unit economics accurately:

- The 120M/month estimate: is that total tokens (prompt + response) or response tokens only? I assume total; please confirm.
- For peak TPS (8): is that concurrent individual requests or aggregated requests to the same API route? (We ask because routing/caching decisions can change cost/latency.)

Next steps from our side:
- Sean will follow up with a preliminary pricing model and target $/1M tokens for the 100-200M band — expect that by tomorrow morning.
- If numbers align, we can schedule a 30-minute soak test next week to validate the 8 TPS peak on our hosted API (no charge for the test).

Thanks — will wait for your quick confirmation on the two clarifying points.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: mutual_action_plan.pdf (updated)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeinc.com>
Date: 2026-03-31T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - pricing qualification and token volume

Quick modeling note for the thread — internal / customer-visible items below so everyone is aligned.

Alex confirmed 120M total tokens / month and 8 TPS peak (avg ~2 TPS). Assuming the 80 prompt / 120 response token averages Alex mentioned, that checks out roughly to the 120M total.

Preliminary unit economics (ballpark for discussion):
- Volume band: 100M-200M tokens / month
- Proposed target list: $40 per 1M tokens (net effective target for initial tier) => $4,800 / month at 120M tokens
- If customer wants committed (reserved capacity) with a 6-12 month commit we can offer volume discounts in the 15-25% range (net $30-$34 / 1M tokens) and provide SLA/priority scaling for peak TPS
- For short soak test / evaluation we can enable hosted API with rate-limits matching 8 TPS and a capped monthly spend (we'll set a $6k cap unless they request otherwise)

Risks/notes:
- If their traffic bursts significantly above the 8 TPS estimate for longer windows we may need to provision additional capacity or recommend moving to a dedicated pool (adds fixed cost but lowers unit price)
- SOC 2: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report with procurement; that typically clears basic procurement gates

Next steps / asks:
- Marissa: share this model with Alex and confirm the 120M is total tokens. If accepted, I'll turn this into a formal quote (line-itemed) and outline the reserved vs. on-demand options.
- Alex: confirm total tokens = prompt + response and whether a capped $6k monthly evaluation spend is acceptable for the soak test.

I can jump on a quick 15-min price review tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
